data.name: Echoed World
data.detailed_description:
Echoed World is a puzzle-based platformer, where mechanics and a story are bound together. The protagonist can no longer create life, but he can still manipulate with what has been already created. This process requires a lot of sacrifices to be made, but is often the only way to traverse through a slowly dying world, where creations are turning against their creator.

Features:

  • Use your powers to overcome platforming puzzles and challenges
  • Explore the captivating world set in an unfamiliar, exotic universe
  • Enjoy traversing the levels with full gamepad support
  • Feast your eyes on distinctive hand-painted graphics
  • Let your experience be enhanced by atmospheric soundtrack

About us:

The game was created as a student project and thus is not very lengthy. Our team decided to put it out for free to get something every starting developer needs –
feedback. Most members of our team had no previous experience with game development and Echoed World was made during a few months of tutored game development classes. Our main goal is to show, what can be achieved with a group of talented, yet inexperienced people in a relatively short amount of time.

We hope that you will enjoy this short, yet sweet adventure.
All the feedback we get on Echoed World will push our team even further!

data.short_description: Experience the epic journey of Algiz, the architect of life, as he seeks to retrieve his stolen power. But not only has his power been stolen. The whole world he designed is on a brink of destruction.

  • Processador: 2.8 GHz Dual Core CPU
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GeForce GT 640, AMD Radeon HD 6750
  • DirectX: Versão 11

reviews.review:
It's a short, free game made by a small student team under tutorage as part of a summer game development project. As long as you keep reminding yourself of that, everything is fine.

A 2D platform-puzzler where you'll control an Architect - beings responsible for creating and shaping planets and the life that inhabits them - you'll drain and restore the life force of your environment in an effort to thwart another, evil architect and his plans to seize ultimate power for himself in a misguided crusade to create things in his own vision of perfection. Honestly, while not being mind-blowing, the story and even the voice acting are better than a lot of other games I've played.

Maybe, like, 95% of the time, this is fairly decent and fun; the hand drawn 2D art is pretty top notch and suitably atmospheric, and the main 3D character model not far behind; the level design and puzzles therein are well crafted enough (even if the puzzles are on the simplistic side); and the audio could easily stand shoulder to shoulder with any other high quality game. But then there is that other 5% of the time when things aren't quite so smooth.

Sometimes the actual hit detection when interacting with a platform can be a bit off and your character will jitter around on the corner of a ledge, not entirely sure whether to grab and hold on, or what to do with it, even just at chest height when running into it. I think I even broke the game somewhat by accidentally making an enemy follow me around a cave when I should have made him fall down a hole, and the game didn't seem to know what to do with me or my progress forcing me to make use of the Restart Level option, losing some collectibles in the process.

But as long as you keep reminding yourself of the mantra that it's a free game made by a small student team, then everything is fine.

This is a really good start. Whether they decide to carry on expanding this game and its universe (especially considering the point the story ends/begins), or work on something completely different, I think it's fair to have high hopes for whatever comes next.
